claim: Let \(C\) be the four-point minimal finite circle and let \(K_{1,0}\) be the sixteen-point Cianci--Ottina minimal finite model of the Klein bottle. The pointwise finite mapping space \(\operatorname{Map}(C,K_{1,0})\) contains exactly \(1{,}288\) order-preserving maps and has exactly \(11\) homotopy components, with sizes \(1{,}024,64,64\), and eight components of size \(17\). Its Stong core is homeomorphic to \(K_{1,0}\sqcup \mathfrak C_4\sqcup \mathfrak C_4\sqcup D_8\), where \(\mathfrak C_4\) is the eight-point crown and \(D_8\) is an eight-point discrete space. More precisely, the \(1{,}024\)-point component retracts by beat-point deletions to the sixteen constant maps, each \(64\)-point component retracts to an eight-point crown, and each \(17\)-point component is contractible.
integrity: The finite enumeration and every beat-point deletion are regenerated by the embedded verifier from the explicitly stated target incidence data. Finite computation is used only for the finite claim stated here; no infinite conclusion is inferred.
scientific_limitations: The result concerns direct maps from the four-point finite circle with no source subdivision.
Only the Cianci--Ottina model K_{1,0} is analyzed; the other minimal Klein-bottle model is outside scope.

title: Mapping-space core from the four-point circle to \(K_{1,0}\)
